title: BSA Runtime Marker
description: Schema for marker JSON files emitted under analysis/runtime/ready/ and analysis/discovery/runtime/ready/. Single source of truth for marker_id alphabet + required payload fields. Canonical documentation: skills/bsa-orchestrator/references/runtime-marker-schema.md. Enforcement points: scripts/validate_marker_chain.py (chain validator) and hooks/pre_write_canonical.sh (write-time validation, US-S5 / F5).

marker_id.description: Filename stem of the marker file (without .json). Closed alphabet — adding a new marker requires a schema change (not a skill-doc change alone).

stage.description: Stage identifier the marker belongs to. Main cycle stages (stage1..stage8), discovery stages (d1..d5), bridge states (discovery.exit, discovery.bridge), end states (handoff, pipeline), Phase-3 dev-handoff stages (phase3.*).

verdict.description: Outcome of the stage/audit this marker represents. READY = stage entry; PASS/FAIL = audit outcome; MERGED = composite-promotion merge marker (e.g., stage1.excerpts.merged reports 'merged' rather than a pass/fail since the merge itself is the event, audit outcomes ride on separate markers); GO/PIVOT/MORE_RESEARCH/NO_GO = discovery-exit decision; PARTIAL = multi-target marker (today: phase3.backlog_exported under --platform=all) where SOME targets succeeded and OTHERS failed (e.g., generic CSV written but Jira write rejected by F5). When verdict=PARTIAL the marker MUST also carry by_platform[] enumerating per-target outcomes — operator reads it to triage which targets to retry. PARTIAL is INTENTIONALLY distinct from FAIL: a fully-failed run emits FAIL with no successful exports; a mixed run emits PARTIAL so the successful artifacts under analysis/handoff/ are not silently treated as if no work happened.

readiness_profile.description: v1.4.0+ (closes review #3.4): readiness scorecard profile that was active when this marker was emitted. Recorded so retroactive review (dashboard / chain validator) can reconstruct WHICH profile gates were applied. Optional — pre-v1.4.0 markers without the field are tolerated as `default`. Most relevant on stage7.skeptical_review.pass / stage8.no_new_claims.pass / handoff.ready / pipeline.complete markers (the gates that actually consume the profile); allowed on any marker so the field can flow through chain-validator passes uniformly.

by_platform.description: v1.3.7+: per-target verdict breakdown for multi-target markers (today: phase3.backlog_exported emitted by bsa-backlog-bridge under --platform=all). REQUIRED when the marker's top-level verdict is PARTIAL — gives the operator a per-platform PASS/FAIL list so they know which targets to retry. Optional when verdict is PASS or FAIL (the operator can infer from CWD inspection of analysis/handoff/backlog_export_*). Out-of-scope for single-target markers (stage*.audit.pass etc.) — those markers MUST NOT carry this field.

platform.description: Backlog target. Closed enum mirroring bsa-backlog-bridge's --platform alphabet (jira/linear/generic) plus github (added by Section C live-API mode in v1.1.6).

verdict.description: Per-target outcome. PASS = export file written + F5-accepted under analysis/handoff/. FAIL = export aborted (write-validator rejection, missing input, etc.). Marker top-level verdict is PARTIAL when this list contains BOTH a PASS and a FAIL; PASS when all are PASS; FAIL when all are FAIL.

reason.description: Optional short operator-facing reason when verdict=FAIL (e.g., 'F5 write-validator rejected backlog_export_jira.json: row STORY-007 missing SourceClaimIDs'). Omit on PASS rows.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC emission time. Pattern enforcement mirrors the `format: date-time` hint because jsonschema's FormatChecker is advisory unless the `jsonschema[format-nongpl]` optional extras are installed (not a documented plugin prereq). H-sec-4 (v1.0.2) added the pattern so malformed timestamps fail regardless of which jsonschema flavor is installed.

canon_policy_version.description: Bare semver ('0.95'), semver+hash ('1.0.0+hash:abc123'), or pre-release form ('1.0.0-rc1+hash:abc123'). Both pre-Sprint-3 and Sprint-3+ workspaces supported.

canon_policy_version_hash.description: SHA-256 prefix of the canon policy byte set. Optional in pre-v1.0 workspaces; mandatory at v1.0.0-rc1 and later. Chain validator tolerates missing hash as 'pre-hash workspace'.

allOf._comment: v1.3.7 R1 fix: PARTIAL is ONLY meaningful for multi-target backlog markers; emitting it on a single-target audit-pass marker is a contract violation. Pre-R1 the verdict enum allowed PARTIAL globally with no constraint — Codex caught it as a MAJOR drift.
v1.3.7 R1 fix: by_platform is the per-target breakdown for multi-target markers. Forbid it on every other marker_id so a stray field on stage1.ready can't masquerade as a backlog gate.

v1.3.7 R1 fix: PARTIAL means MIXED — both PASS and FAIL must appear in by_platform. All-PASS or all-FAIL with verdict=PARTIAL is a contract violation (use PASS or FAIL respectively). Enforced via two anyOf conditions: at least one PASS row AND at least one FAIL row.

x-bsa-audit-pass-sequence._comment: Audit-pass sequences used by scripts/validate_marker_chain.py for chain-gating checks. NOT the full marker alphabet — only the mandatory gate markers that form the promotion chain. Ready markers (stage*.ready) and end-state markers (handoff.ready, pipeline.complete) are in the marker_id alphabet above but not part of the gating sequence.

x-bsa-ready-markers._comment: Stage-ready markers (emitted by orchestrator when a stage becomes workable). Informational — validators accept these as valid but do not gate on them.

x-bsa-end-state-markers._comment: Terminal markers. handoff.ready is emitted after stage8 promote as the gate into handoff packaging. pipeline.complete is emitted after /bsa-handoff (main-cycle terminal). phase3.backlog_exported is emitted after bsa-backlog-bridge writes the requested platform exports under analysis/handoff/. pipeline.phase3.complete is the Phase-3 terminal marker — emitted at the end of a full /bsa-dev-handoff chain (NOT under --only=backlog-bridge).

x-bsa-bridge-markers._comment: Cross-chain bridge markers. bsa.stage1.entry.enabled is emitted after discovery.go to allow main-cycle stage1 activation.

x-bsa-decision-markers._comment: Discovery-exit decision markers. Exactly one of these is emitted at D-Exit.
